en: Although invisible, air is a mixture of gases that has measurable mass and takes up physical space inside a balloon.
Melting uses heat to change solid ice into liquid water, whereas dissolving mixes solid sugar into liquid tea without heat.
Puddles dry up because liquid water evaporates into a gas at room temperature, not just when it reaches a boiling point.
Rusting iron is a chemical change because the metal reacts with oxygen to form a completely new, flaky substance.
The air we breathe is a gaseous solution of nitrogen and oxygen, proving that solutions are not always liquid.
Boiling water to make bubbles is a physical change because the resulting steam is still the exact same chemical substance.
A giant steel ship floats while a small steel nail sinks because the ship's overall density is lower than water.
Solid ice and liquid water are the exact same chemical substance, merely existing in different physical states of matter.
You can separate a mixture of sand and water using physical filtration, proving that mixtures do not require chemical reactions to separate.
Mercury is a metallic element that exists as a liquid at room temperature, showing that not all metals are solid.
Chopping a log into smaller pieces is a physical change because the smaller wood pieces remain chemically identical to the original log.
Water droplets forming on a cold glass come from water vapor in the air condensing, not from liquid leaking through the glass.
